solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Could join Mensa and is tempted

definitions.meaning: Mensa admits only the very clever, so someone who could join has a fine intellect
to be inclined or half-minded to do something, as in the idiom with 'to' after it

explanation.surface: Someone bright enough for Mensa is thinking of signing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense describes intelligence; the second is the idiom 'to have a good mind to do something', meaning to feel strongly inclined.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings are idioms: one praises intellect, the other expresses an urge or inclination to act.

clue.text: Gather shaver is broken. I dropped it

indicators.note: the shaver is broken into pieces, so its letters are rearranged
the letter I is dropped from the little word 'it'

explanation.surface: Someone's razor broke because they dropped it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I dropped it' removes I from IT, leaving T; 'is broken' rearranges SHAVER plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in a crop is to gather it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Assembles the article for ship's cargo

indicators.note: what is carried inside the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship
IT, a word for the thing in question

explanation.surface: Someone gathers the goods to be loaded as a ship's freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembles' looks like putting together a load, but it is the verb for a parliament convening.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament or court is said to sit when it convenes, so it is a synonym for assembles.

clue.text: Try, with primitive weapon, to get bird

parts.note: to have a go is to try
a sling hurls stones, as David used against Goliath

explanation.surface: Try catching a bird with an ancient weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is a specific kind of bird, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Sequel to 'September Song' that brings the sea to mind?

definitions.text: that brings the sea to mind?

parts.note: October follows September, abbreviated OCT
an opus is a musical work

explanation.surface: A follow-up to a famous ballad that evokes the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'September Song' reads as a song title, but split it: what follows September, then a musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-armed sea creature would naturally make one think of the ocean, a loose cryptic description.

clue.text: Correspondence Irishman returned

indicators.note: the name comes back, reading upwards in this down entry

parts.note: Liam is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: Letters arrive from an Irishman who has come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses LIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and parcels sent by post are synonymous with correspondence.

clue.text: Two necessities for tennis, as a game

parts.note: the first of the two things every tennis match needs is the mesh across the court
the second tennis essential is the thing hit back and forth

explanation.surface: Listing the two essentials of tennis, as if for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two necessities for tennis' supplies both pieces together: the mesh strung across the court and the object that is struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport, similar to basketball, played mainly in Britain and the Commonwealth.

clue.text: First delivery (or address number one)

definitions.meaning: the first speech delivered, as in a debate or trial
the first address or talk given

explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' looks like the post, but a speech is delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe the initial formal talk given to an audience, delivered first.

clue.text: Law examination paper

parts.note: not a test paper for law students, but a legal document authorising police to examine premises

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests an exam for law students; the examination is a police search.
explanation.definitionFit: A court-issued document allowing the police to search a property is literally a legal paper for an examination.

clue.text: Goody-goody scolds baddies

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for sanctimonious
to rate someone is an old verb for berating them

explanation.surface: A prim, virtuous type tells off the villains.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning to scold is an old-fashioned sense, still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea robbers are the stock villains of adventure stories, so they serve as an example of baddies.

clue.text: Order the first student to come in

indicators.note: says the following pieces enter the word before them

parts.note: 1ST, with the figure one read as the letter I
L, the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: An instruction that the leading student should enter the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is written 1ST, read as IST. 'Order' looks like a command but is a noun: the Order of the Thistle is Scotland's chivalric order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry.

clue.text: Newly-wed making ends meet, in poverty

indicators.note: the middle is cut out so the two ends of the hyphenated word join up

explanation.surface: A newly married couple struggling to make ends meet while poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making ends meet' removes WLYW from the middle of NEWLYWED, leaving the first two and last two letters, NE and ED, joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Need is a noun for want or destitution, a synonym of poverty, as in 'families in need'.

clue.text: Double-page insert in 'Home Repairs' that's not all there

indicators.note: says the pages go inside the home repairs

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, covers home repairs

indicators.note: says the page letter appears twice over

explanation.surface: A two-page spread inserted in a home improvement magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: DIY, do-it-yourself, is British shorthand for home repairs and improvements.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of calling someone scatty or a bit silly in the head.

clue.text: Not raining, I will take long way round

indicators.note: the long way goes round the letter I

parts.note: far means a long way off

explanation.surface: It's dry, so I'll take the long route on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts I inside FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is fine and dry, describing a day without rain.

clue.text: Getting mouth round sibilant, is unsuccessful

definitions.text: Getting mouth round sibilant, is unsuccessful

indicators.note: the mouth word goes round the letter

parts.note: the lips form the mouth
S is the classic hissing sibilant

explanation.surface: Someone trying to pronounce an S sound and failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts S inside LIPS. The whole clue also describes the speech impediment.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a lisp cannot shape S sounds properly, failing to get their tongue around sibilants.

clue.text: Woman's named this price that's very low

definitions.meaning: a single coin of the lowest value, so a very cheap price

explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, and the smallest British coin, so a trifling cost.

clue.text: Back on night shifts, love

indicators.note: says the little word that follows is read backwards
the letters of 'night' shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker is back on night shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns ON into NO; 'shifts' rearranges NIGHT into THING. In tennis, love means a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is a tennis score of zero, so it means none at all.

clue.text: Having slate loose, thought 'Ought to quit to become kind of fighter'

indicators.note: the letters are set loose and rearranged
the word 'Ought' leaves 'thought', taking its letters out

explanation.surface: A worried roofer with a loose slate wonders about joining the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ought to quit' takes OUGHT from THOUGHT, leaving TH; 'loose' rearranges SLATE plus TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A stealth fighter is a military jet built to evade radar detection.

clue.text: Fought, getting quietly ejected — inflicted minor injuries

indicators.note: says the quiet letter is thrown out

parts.note: scrapped, in the informal sense of had a scrap or fight
P, piano, the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone got into a fight, was thrown out, and came away with cuts and bruises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejected' removes P from SCRAPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To graze the skin is to cause a small injury, a typical playground hurt.

clue.text: Rake money in, as usual

indicators.note: the money goes inside the rake

parts.note: a roue is a dissolute man, a rake
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Raking in the money, as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a verb with 'money in', but it is the noun for a libertine, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means ordinary or customary, a synonym for usual.

clue.text: Draft a grid, new, in the morning

indicators.note: the letters are made new by rearranging them

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Someone drafting a new grid early in the day, perhaps a setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges A GRID into DIAGR.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft can be a sketch or plan, and a plan drawn on paper is a type of drawing.

clue.text: For retirement, a little spot outside N Western US state

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: AN, the indefinite article in its other form

indicators.note: the particle goes round the N

parts.note: an atom is a tiny particle or speck
N, taken from the clue as it stands

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a little place outside a northern town to retire to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives AN, the article's other form; 'outside' puts the particle round N, and 'For retirement' turns everything backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Montana is a large mountainous state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: Signs by which doctor is not perturbed

parts.note: MO, medical officer

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Symptoms that leave the doctor unworried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perturbed' rearranges IS NOT into TIONS. 'not perturbed' reads as calm, but 'not' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures made with the hand are signs, so both mean movements that communicate.

clue.text: Some random person that the snatchers were after?

definitions.meaning: split as two words, any corpse was what grave-robbing body snatchers wanted

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means whoever at all; split in two it is any corpse sought by grave robbers.

clue.text: Going back, add note to 'American Birds'

indicators.note: says the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: to sum is to add up figures
E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: An instruction to add a note to a book called American Birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going back' reverses SUM + E. The birds are Australian, not American, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds, so they are an example of the plural noun.

clue.text: Shoots game

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means moves or shoots swiftly
a pub game of throwing small arrows at a board

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for rapid movement; the other is the popular pub game played with arrows and a board.

clue.text: Socialist revolutionary seizes Yankee, one who could change silver into gold?

definitions.text: one who could change silver into gold?

indicators.note: the reversed word grabs and holds the letter
the socialist word revolves, reading backwards

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist
Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A socialist revolutionary captures an American, then turns alchemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses RED to DER; 'seizes' puts Y inside. The definition sounds like alchemy but means changing a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who colours fabric could turn silver-coloured cloth golden, a playful description of the trade.

clue.text: Mark beats up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tops means beats or outdoes

explanation.surface: A man named Mark beats someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or stain, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Very cold duck

definitions.meaning: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Zero degrees is freezing point; in cricket, a batsman out without scoring makes a duck, a score of nothing.

clue.text: Happy golfer taking easy shot to green?

definitions.text: golfer taking easy shot to green?
definitions.meaning: a player making a short lofted shot onto the putting surface

explanation.surface: A cheerful golfer playing a short approach shot.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an informal adjective for cheerful; the other describes someone who plays a chip shot in golf.

clue.text: Anagram done — have to finish clue after next

indicators.note: puts the 'have' word at the end
here the word plainly signals that 'done' is to be rearranged

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: A solver notes the anagram is done and must finish the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue after the next one (30 across) is the first down clue, so the definition refers to the grid itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In clue order the entry following the final across clue is the first of the downs, so it is self-referential.

clue.text: Latest thing in child entertainment

parts.note: 'Latest' means last in the day, not newest: the final treat before a child sleeps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Latest thing' suggests a new fad, but it means the last thing at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale read aloud to a child at the end of the day is the final entertainment before sleep.
